draft.emotion: matter-of-fact and straightforward, describing a basic quality
notes: Do not confuse with 'tối', which means 'dark' in the sense of lacking light (e.g. a dark room or night).
In spoken Vietnamese, 'đen' is also commonly used to mean 'unlucky' (short for 'đen đủi').

faults.why: Vietnamese 'đ' is implosive /ɗ/, not /d/, and tone is missing.

faults.quote: The darkest colour, absorbing all light and reflecting none.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('The darkest colour') and uses overly technical language.

faults.quote: (light) Lacking light; very dark or gloomy.
faults.why: 'Lacking light' is 'tối', not 'đen'; 'đen' means dark-skinned/tanned or (colloquially) unlucky.
Unnatural; 'trời tối quá' is used for a dark night, 'trời đen kịt' for storm clouds.
